draft.change: Add the Syriac spelling and its defining verse to the root article for Jesse.
draft.definition: אִישַי is the Syriac name of Jesse, David’s father.
draft.evidence: Matthew 1:6 names אִישַי as the father of David, the same relationship given for Hebrew יִשַׁי in Ruth 4:17.

analysis.evidence: אִישַי אַולֵדֿ לדַֿוִידֿ מַלכָּא means “Jesse fathered David the king.” The verb אַולֵדֿ identifies Jesse as the father, and the prefixed ל on David marks the son.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name, with no prefix or suffix. It is the subject of אַולֵדֿ.
analysis.sense: Jesse, the father of King David.

analysis.evidence: Jesse (אִישַי) is the subject of אַולֵדֿ, and the prefixed ל marks David the king (לדַֿוִידֿ מַלכָּא) as its object. The clause identifies Jesse as David’s father.
analysis.morphology: Aphel perfect, third person masculine singular, without a pronominal suffix.

draft.change: Add the pointed Syriac spelling as a name article linked to the same root and bearer as the Hebrew David article.
draft.definition: The Syriac form of the personal name David.
draft.evidence: Matthew 1:6 identifies the bearer by his father Jesse, his title “king,” and his son Solomon.

analysis.evidence: אִישַי אַולֵדֿ לדַֿוִידֿ names David as the son Jesse fathered. מַלכָּא identifies him as king. The next clause repeats his name without the prefix, דַּוִידֿ, as the father of Solomon.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with prefixed ל marking the direct object of אַולֵדֿ.
analysis.sense: The personal name of King David, Jesse’s son and Solomon’s father.

analysis.evidence: In אִישַי אַולֵדֿ לדַֿוִידֿ מַלכָּא, “Jesse fathered David the king,” מַלכָּא stands in apposition to David and gives his royal title.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the emphatic state, with no prefix or pronominal suffix.

draft.change: Add the pointed Syriac spelling דַּוִידֿ as a name entry linked to the same root as Hebrew דָּוִד.
draft.definition: The Syriac personal name of King David, Jesse’s son and Solomon’s father.
draft.evidence: Matthew 1:6 repeats David’s name where the genealogy moves from Jesse fathering David to David fathering Solomon.

analysis.evidence: The first clause names David as Jesse’s son and calls him מַלכָּא, “the king.” The marked occurrence opens the next clause, דַּוִידֿ אַולֵדֿ לַשלֵימָונ, “David fathered Solomon.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name, unprefixed and unsuffixed, serving as the subject of אַולֵדֿ.
analysis.sense: David, the king who was Jesse’s son and Solomon’s father.

analysis.evidence: At position 5, דַּוִידֿ (David) is the subject of אַולֵדֿ, and לַשלֵימָונ marks Solomon as its object. David fathered Solomon by Uriah’s wife.
analysis.morphology: Aphel perfect, third person masculine singular

draft.change: Add a name article for the Syriac spelling שלֵימָונ, linked to the same root and bearer as the Hebrew spelling שְׁלֹמֹה.
draft.definition: The Syriac personal name of Solomon, son of David.
draft.evidence: Matthew 1:6 identifies the bearer by his parentage. First Chronicles 22:9 connects his Hebrew name with the peace promised during his lifetime, supporting the root שלמ.

analysis.evidence: In דַּוִידֿ אַולֵדֿ לַשלֵימָונ, David is the father and Solomon is the child. The following phrase מֵנ אַנ_תּתֵֿה דֻּאורִיָא identifies the mother as Uriah’s wife.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with prefixed לַ marking the direct object of אַולֵדֿ (“fathered”).
analysis.sense: Solomon, the son of David by Uriah’s wife.

analysis.evidence: In מֵנ אַנ_תּתֵֿה דֻּאורִיָא, “by the wife of Uriah,” the possessive suffix anticipates Uriah, who is named in the following ד־phrase. The relationship identifies the woman as Uriah’s wife.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular noun with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Uriah linked to the light root אור.
draft.definition: The personal name Uriah, here borne by the Hittite whose wife was Bathsheba.
draft.evidence: Matthew 1:6 calls Solomon’s mother the wife of Uriah. Second Samuel 11:3 identifies the couple by name.

evidence.note: David fathers Solomon by the woman identified as the wife of אֻורִיָא.
Bathsheba is identified as the wife of אוּרִיָּה the Hittite.
The words “Yahweh is my light” pair the divine name with אוֹרִי, “my light”, illustrating the proposed meaning of the name.

article.name: אֻורִיָא
article.summary: Matthew names Uriah the Hittite when he identifies Solomon’s mother as Uriah’s wife. The Syriac name represents Hebrew אוּרִיָּה, traditionally understood as “Yahweh is my light”.

conflicts: resolve the bearer and validate its name article against the current lexicon

analysis.evidence: In מֵנ אַנ_תּתֵֿה דֻּאורִיָא, “by the wife of Uriah”, the suffix on “wife” anticipates the husband named after דּ־. Matthew identifies Solomon’s mother through Uriah. Second Samuel 11:3 names her as Bathsheba, wife of Uriah the Hittite.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with prefixed genitive particle דּ־, “of”.
